Protect Yourself

  1. Close observation to tell if you're going to be a mild case (and can be sent home to quarantine & ride it out, reducing load on the hospitals & possibly financial load on you), or whether you're going to be a critical case that will need hospital-grade support. Monitoring of blood-oxygen levels (and acting when they started to drop) was part of China's diagnostic heuristic, etc.
  2. Close monitoring and/or shoring-up of other comorbidities. If you're diabetic, for example, or have congested arteries or a history of COPD or are immunocompromised, etc, they can / you could scale up your rigor or treatment of those so that if your condition worsens, your body doesn't have to do that extra work.
  3. The obvious, ventilator support if necessary.
  4. Getting you on "the list" for other experimental or cutting-edge treatments. For example, plasma transfusions from recovered patients were reported to significantly help the recovery of patients in China. They won't even consider you for that treatment if you don't have SARS-nCoV-2 because it won't help with anything else. And so on, as more treatments are discovered.

Protect Others

  1. If you have SARS-nCoV-2, you get priority for a face mask to reduce your spreading of it. Given the shortage, no masks for the cold, no masks for the flu, no masks on healthy people - but if you've got The Bug, you get a mask.
  2. Contact tracing. If you know you have it, any high-risk individuals that you were in contact with can be found and brought into awareness & preparedness (and treatment or quarantine) so that they don't just show up at the hospital in their dying throes when it's too late.
  3. Medical understanding. How it spreads, what kills it, who's most at-risk, is it mutating, how does it work, what exactly does it attack, etc - all of that requires good data with good sample sizes. If you're tested and know you have it, your medical story can contribute to the greater understanding - though probably nobody will reap the benefits of that until much later.
